name: Curitiba
author: knoxio
description:
# Curitiba · CWB The city that invented bus rapid transit instead of building a metro. Curitiba's 1974 *eixos estruturais* — dedicated bus lanes, tube stations, pre-paid boarding — became the model copied by Bogotá, Istanbul and Jakarta, and are the reason the city never laid rail. The 2022 census records **0.0% of commutes by train or metro**, against 26.5% by bus and 49.8% by car. Build the metro Curitiba never built. ![Jardim Botânico de Curitiba](gallery/screenshot1.webp) ## Coverage
RegionGreater Curitiba, Paraná (BR) — 17 municipalities
Bounding Box-49.55, -25.72 → -48.95, -25.15
Playable Area~3,797 km²
## Population Summary
Census Population (2022)3,271,037

## Map Statistics
Buildings Indexed1,016,715
Demand Points19,659
Population Nodes64,354
Median Commute Distance9.3 km
Mean Commute Distance11.2 km
## Methodology Demand is built entirely from Brazilian government sources — no OSM population estimation. 1. **Residents.** IBGE Censo 2022 census tracts (5,623 tracts, 3,271,037 people) disaggregated onto individual dwelling addresses from CNEFE, the national address register. 1,388,241 dwelling units placed — 99.90% of the census household count. Each CNEFE row is one dwelling *unit*, so a tower appears as up to 540 rows at one coordinate and the distribution reproduces census household size by construction. 2. **Jobs.** IBGE CEMPRE 2024 municipal employment totals distributed across 148,690 establishment addresses from CNEFE, weighted by type inferred from each establishment's recorded description. 3. **Commutes.** Doubly-constrained gravity model with the deterrence function *and* the travel-time model fitted jointly to the observed car-commute time distribution from Censo 2022 table 10330 (χ² 0.0071). All 46,709 distinct pairs routed through OSRM. 4. **Special demand.** 57 places — Afonso Pena airport, 18 university campuses, 4 stadiums, 10 shopping centres, 10 hospitals, 7 parks, the zoo and cultural venues. BRT terminals are deliberately excluded: a terminal is somewhere people pass through rather than a trip end, and including it would both double-count and pre-commit the player to the corridors URBS already chose. 5. **Schools.** INEP's Censo Escolar 2024 gives real per-school enrolment for 2,051 active schools in the extent (680,403 enrolments), geocoded by joining each school's postcode to CNEFE — 79% land on an address CNEFE already records as an education establishment. Travel fractions by level (infantil 0.20 through médio 0.85) reflect that a six-year-old does not travel independently. Commuting is a minority of urban travel, so a map built only from a journey-to-work matrix under-represents exactly the destinations a player wants to serve; the final split is 64.6% commute, 20.0% special destinations, 15.3% education. 6. **Tiles and buildings.** Overture footprints (OSM has only 87k in this extent against Overture's 1.32M), with heights borrowed from OSM where available. The `commercial` district layer comes from IPPUC's statutory zoning rather than OSM land use, and neighbourhood labels from Curitiba's 75 official bairros. ## Additional Features - **Water depth profiles** — reservoirs and lakes carry a graded bed rather than a flat one. Per-body mean depths come from HydroLAKES (13 bodies inside the extent) and are split into concentric bands, so a crossing near the bank is feasible where one through the deep centre is not. Depths run from −1.5 m at the margins to −22.6 m in the deepest reservoir centre. - **Building Collision** — 1,016,715 indexed footprints with height data, shipped in both binary and legacy JSON form so the pack installs on any game version. - **Statutory zoning** — the 1.5 commercial/college district tint is driven by Curitiba's actual zoning law (LEI 15511/2019), not by inferred land use. - **Official neighbourhoods** — all 75 IPPUC bairros labelled. - **Roads & Runways** — 59,132 road ways plus Afonso Pena and Bacacheri airport geometry. --- _Cover photo: Jardim Botânico de Curitiba by [jerzykwpodrozy](https://pixabay.com/users/jerzykwpodrozy-16143839/) via Pixabay._ _Water depths derived from [HydroLAKES](https://www.hydrosheds.org/products/hydrolakes) (Messager et al. 2016), CC BY 4.0._
